name: sfsr-rems
description: St. Francis Square Realty Real Estate Management System — monorepo root

scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test

comment:overrides: jose is pinned to the 5 line, and this is the actual fix for the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM described below — engines.node alone was not. firebase-admin@14 -> jwks-rsa@4.1.0 does `const jose = require('jose')` on line 1 of src/utils.js. jose@6's exports map has NO `require` condition (only `default: ./dist/webapi/index.js`, which is ESM), so that require can ONLY resolve on a runtime with require(esm) — Node >=20.19 or >=22.12, exactly what jwks-rsa declares in its own engines. Depending on the host to give us that Node version is a bet we lost in production: Vercel served ERR_REQUIRE_ESM on every request even with engines pinned to 22.x. jose@5.10.0 still ships a real CommonJS build (`require: ./dist/node/cjs/index.js`), so the require resolves on ANY runtime and the Node floor stops being load-bearing. jwks-rsa touches only importJWK, exportSPKI and decodeJwt, all of which are unchanged in v5. Declared in apps/portal as well: npm honours `overrides` only in the package.json at the ROOT of the install tree, and Vercel's Root Directory is apps/portal, so the root copy alone is not read there.
comment:engines: 22.x, raised from >=20.11 — and that old floor was the bug behind a production 500. firebase-admin@14 -> jwks-rsa@4.1.0 is CommonJS and does `require('jose')` on line 1 of src/utils.js, while jose@6 dropped CommonJS entirely: its exports map has no `require` condition, only an ESM `default`. That combination only loads on a runtime that can require() an ES module — Node >=20.19 or >=22.12, which is exactly what jwks-rsa declares in its OWN engines field. Local Node 22.14 has it enabled by default, so every build and test passed here; Vercel's serverless runtime was older and every request died with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. Pinned to the 22 line rather than the full `^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=23` range, because that is the form Vercel reads when selecting a runtime and it is the line this project is actually tested on. Declared in BOTH apps as well as here: with Vercel's Root Directory set to apps/portal, that is the package.json it reads.
